q: 211. Which of the following trees yields hard wood?
explain: Shisham is a hardwood (from broad-leaved trees). Deodar, chir and pine are softwoods from conifers.

q: 212. Stainless steel contains .....
explain: The common 18/8 stainless steel has about 18% chromium and 8% nickel.

q: 213. Cast iron contains carbon approximately .....
explain: As per the answer key, option a. Note: cast iron is usually quoted as about 2 to 4.5% carbon, so the printed range is wide.

q: 214. Settle contains carbon approximately .....
explain: 'Settle' is a misprint for steel in the book. Steel contains about 0.05 to 1.75% carbon.

q: 215. Wrought iron contains carbon about .....
explain: Wrought iron contains about 0.15% carbon (up to 0.15%).

q: 216. Mild steel is used for .....
options: structural works in beams, joints and girders
explain: Mild steel is used in structural members such as beams, joists and girders.

q: 217. Wrought iron is used for .....
explain: Wrought iron is used for small water pipes, railings and similar items.

q: 218. The frog of a brick is normally made on its .....
explain: As per the answer key, the frog is made on the top face.

q: 219. Slacking of lime is affected by .....
explain: As per the answer key, slaking is done by adding water, i.e. immersing the lime in water.

q: 220. Lime mortar is generally made with .....
explain: As per the answer key, hydraulic lime is generally used for lime mortar.

q: 221. The commonly used lime in white-washing, is .....
explain: Fat lime, being pure and white, is commonly used for white-washing.

q: 222. Lime concrete is generally used for .....
explain: As per the answer key, option b. Note: lime concrete is also used for wall foundations, so this key answer looks doubtful.

q: 223. The minimum percentage of silica, alumina and ferric oxide in lime for white washing, is .....
explain: Fat lime for white-washing is pure, so it needs no clayey impurities; the minimum is 0.

q: 224. The initial setting time of hydraulic lime, is .....
explain: As per the answer key, the initial setting time of hydraulic lime is 120 minutes.

q: 225. The initial setting time of lime-pozzolana, is .....
explain: As per the answer key, the initial setting time of lime-pozzolana is 120 minutes.

q: 226. The steel used for the manufacture of rails, is .....
explain: As per the answer key, Bessemer steel is used for rails.

q: 227. Which of the following is a rock?
explain: Quartz, mica and gypsum are minerals; a rock is an aggregate of minerals, so none of these is a rock.

q: 228. Which of the following metamorphic rocks has the most weather resisting characteristics?
explain: Quartzite is hard and made of silica, so it resists weathering best. Limestone is sedimentary, not metamorphic.

q: 229. A good building stone should not absorb water more than .....
explain: As per the answer key, a good building stone should not absorb more than 5% water.

q: 230. Which of the following has more fire resisting characteristics?
explain: As per the answer key, compact sandstone resists fire better than marble, limestone or granite, which crack or calcine at high heat.

q: 231. Jumper is a tool used for .....
explain: A jumper is a long steel bar used to bore holes in rock for blasting during quarrying.

q: 232. The important test to be conducted on a stone used in docks and harbours is .....
explain: As per the answer key, option c (weight test). The bottom of this page is cut off in the scan, so options a and b are not fully readable. Please check them against your copy.

q: 233. The filler used in plastic bitumen, is .....
explain: As per the answer key, asbestos powder is used as the filler. (The book prints 'tale' for talc in option b.)

q: 234. The commonly used raw material in the manufacture of cement, is .....
explain: Limestone provides the lime, the main raw material of cement.

q: 235. The compound of Portland cement which contributes to the strength after two to three years is .....
explain: Di-calcium silicate hydrates slowly and keeps adding strength for years.

q: 236. Rapid hardening cement attains early strength due to .....
options: larger proportion of lime grounded liner than normal cement
lesser proportion of lime grounded coarser than normal cement
lesser proportion of lime grounded finer than normal cement
larger proportion of lime grounded coarser than normal cement
explain: Rapid hardening cement has more lime (C3S) and is ground finer ('liner' is a misprint for 'finer'), so it gains strength early.

q: 237. The rock with poorest strength is .....
explain: Shale is a weak, soft sedimentary rock.

q: 238. The rocks formed from molten magma, are called .....
explain: Rocks formed from molten magma are igneous rocks.

q: 239. The rocks formed by gradual deposition, are called .....
explain: Gradual deposition of materials forms sedimentary rocks.

q: 240. Rocks formed due to alternation of original structure due to heat and excessive pressure, are called .....
explain: Alteration of original structure by heat and pressure forms metamorphic rocks.

q: 241. Lime stones are generally known as .....
explain: Limestone is sedimentary, so it is also called aqueous or stratified rock.

q: 242. Geologically, marble is known as .....
explain: Marble is a metamorphic rock formed from limestone.

q: 243. Chemically, marble is known as .....
explain: Marble is mainly calcium carbonate, so chemically it is a calcareous rock.

q: 244. Kaolin is chemically classified as .....
explain: Kaolin is a pure white clay, so it is argillaceous.

q: 245. Basalt is .....
explain: Basalt forms from lava on the surface, so it is extrusive (volcanic).

q: 246. Sand stone is .....
explain: Sandstone is a sedimentary rock made of cemented sand grains.

q: 247. Lime stone is not a .....
explain: Limestone is sedimentary (stratified, aqueous); it is not a metamorphic rock.

q: 248. Cast iron is used for .....
explain: Cast iron is strong in compression, so it is used for columns and struts.

q: 249. Cross cut saw is used for .....
explain: As per the answer key, option b. Note: a cross cut saw is more commonly linked with cutting soft stones, so this key answer looks doubtful.

q: 250. The most common admixture which is used to accelerate the initial set of concrete is .....
explain: Calcium chloride is the most common accelerator for concrete.

q: 251. Due to attack of dry rot, the timber .....
explain: Dry rot reduces timber to powder.

q: 252. Teak wood is suitable for .....
explain: As per the answer key, option b. Note: teak is also used for sleepers, so the key answer is debatable.

q: 253. Seasoning of timber is done for .....
explain: Seasoning is done to decrease the moisture content of timber.

q: 254. Veneering means .....
options: carving out designs on timber planks
thick layer of superior wood glued to inferior wood
thin layer of superior wood glued to inferior wood
explain: Veneering is gluing a thin layer of superior wood on an inferior wood base.

q: 255. Which of the following has the lowest crushing strength?
explain: Laterite is a soft, porous rock, so it has the lowest crushing strength here.

q: 256. The rocks having alumina or clay as their major constituents, are known as .....
explain: Rocks with alumina or clay as the major constituent are argillaceous.

q: 257. The hardest rock is .....
explain: As per the answer key, quartz, since diamond is a mineral, not a rock. (The book prints 'tale' for talc.)

q: 258. The softest rock is .....
explain: Talc is the softest of these (hardness 1 on Mohs' scale).

q: 259. The Specific gravity of marble is .....
explain: As per the answer key, the specific gravity of marble is 2.72.

q: 260. Shingle is .....
explain: As per the answer key, option a. Note: this contradicts Q136, where shingle is water-bound pebbles, so one of the two key answers is likely an error in the book.

q: 261. The rock generally used for roofing, is .....
explain: Slate splits into thin, light, water-resistant sheets, so it is used for roofing.

q: 262. Good quality stones must .....
explain: A good stone must be durable, free from clay and resistant to acids.

q: 263. A limestone found in seams of great thickness in non-crystalline texture with earthy appearance is called .....
explain: Compact limestone has a non-crystalline, earthy texture and occurs in thick seams.

q: 264. A limestone containing about 30% of alumina and silica is called .....
explain: Kankar is an impure limestone that contains clayey matter and is used to make hydraulic lime.

q: 265. The compressive strength of sandstone is .....
explain: As per the answer key, the compressive strength of sandstone is 65 MN/m².

q: 266. The specific gravity of sandstone is .....
explain: As per the answer key, the specific gravity of sandstone is 2.65 to 2.95.

q: 267. High alumina cement is produced by fusing together a mixture of .....
options: limestone, gypsum, bauxite, clay and chalk
explain: High alumina cement is made by fusing limestone and bauxite.

q: 268. King closers are related to .....
explain: King closers are special brick shapes used in brick masonry.

q: 269. Surkhi is added to lime mortar to .....
explain: Surkhi is a pozzolana; it gives hydraulic properties to lime mortar.

q: 270. The role of super plasticizers in a cement paste is to .....
options: disperse the particles and to remove air bubbles
disperse the particles, removes air bubbles and to retard setting
explain: As per the answer key, option c. Super plasticizers disperse cement particles, release trapped air and can retard setting.

q: 271. In the cement the compound quickest to react with water, is .....
explain: Tricalcium aluminate (C3A) reacts fastest with water.

q: 272. Rapid hardening cement contains .....
explain: Rapid hardening cement contains more tri-calcium silicate (C3S), which gives early strength.

q: 273. Generally wooden moulds are made from .....
explain: As per the answer key, shisham wood, which is hard and durable. (The book prints 'play wood' in option a.)

q: 274. The kiln which may work throughout the year, is .....
explain: Hoffman's kiln is a continuous kiln and can work throughout the year.

q: 275. The lime which contains mainly calcium oxide and slacks with water is .....
explain: As per the answer key, quick lime, which is mainly calcium oxide and slakes with water.

q: 276. Excess of silica in the clay .....
options: makers the brick brittle and weak
makes the brick crack and warp on drying
changes colour of the brick from red to yellow
improves impermeability and durability of the brick
explain: As per the answer key, excess silica makes the brick brittle and weak. (The book prints 'makers'.)

q: 277. Which of the following constituent, when present in excess quantity in clay causes the bricks to melt and distort during burning?
explain: As per the answer key, lime. Excess lime melts the clay in burning and distorts the bricks (alkalies also act as a flux, but the key gives c).

q: 278. The alkaline salt present in the bricks, absorbs moisture from the air which on drying .....
options: leaves pores and makes the bricks porous
leaves high powder deposit on the brick
makes the bricks brittle and weak
explain: As per the answer key, option b. Alkali salts absorb moisture and on drying leave a powdery deposit (efflorescence).

q: 279. The good clay for making bricks is .....
explain: Weathered clay is more plastic and uniform, so it is good for bricks.

q: 280. The process of mixing clay, water and other ingredients to make bricks, is known as .....
explain: As per the answer key, kneading. Note: other questions in the book use 'tempering' or 'pugging' for this operation.
